1|town-court|Margot,Clerk@medium@Adult fictional guide Margot speaks across the desk while Clerk picks up a quill.|-@insert@The quill touches a fresh parchment sheet beside the ordinary inkpot.|Margot@close_up@Margot watches the clerk off frame with a serious expectant expression.|-@insert@One sealed folded petition lies beside a partly filled register, abstract marks only and no legible text.

2|court-street|Margot@wide@Margot approaches the ordinary court entrance in the modest town street.|Margot@medium@Margot pauses before the door holding a single folded petition.|-@insert@The stone doorway, bench and ordinary iron latch remain fixed, no guards, chains or weapons.|Margot@close_up@Margot takes a steady breath and prepares to enter, dignified and fully clothed.

3|town-court|Margot,Clerk@medium@Clerk listens while Margot explains her account with a restrained hand gesture.|Clerk@close_up@Clerk looks from the speaker to the page before writing.|-@insert@Two plain parchment entries lie beside the quill with abstract marks and no readable testimony.|Margot@close_up@Margot carefully clarifies a detail without tears or visible injury.

4|records-room|-@wide@The empty records room contains shelves of tied bundles and a plain work desk.|-@insert@A folded parchment with an unlettered wax seal lies on the desk.|-@close_up@The bound register is open to abstract handwritten-looking lines, no counterfeit quote.|-@insert@A narrow strip of blank parchment rests beside a closed bundle, showing only a fragment of a larger record.

5|town-court|Margot,Judge@medium@Margot stands at the clerk's desk while Judge listens from the established back bench.|-@insert@An open plain legal book and a closed petition rest apart on the desk.|Clerk@medium@Clerk checks a second document before continuing the entry.|Margot@close_up@Margot waits seriously for an explanation of the next step.

6|records-room|-@insert@An illustrative English case roll is unrolled on the records desk, no title, date or readable quotation.|-@close_up@Two separate folded parchment submissions lie side by side, one with a simple broken wax seal.|-@insert@A second inquiry bundle has been opened beside the original roll, no people.|-@close_up@An ordinary empty purse and two small unmarked counters lie beside the closed case bundle, symbolic of recorded payments.

7|records-room|-@insert@The first petition is set on one side of the desk while a second inquiry roll remains open.|Clerk@close_up@One mitten hand from Clerk points from the first roll toward the second, body mostly cropped.|Clerk@medium@Clerk compares the two bundles at the desk without treating them as identical cases.|-@insert@The unrolled second sheet is placed above the first, visually showing continuation rather than disappearance.

8|court-street|Margot@medium@Margot leaves the court doorway carrying her folded papers.|Margot@close_up@Margot looks uncertain about whether she will have to return.|Agnes,Margot@medium@Agnes listens supportively on the public bench beside Margot.|Agnes,Margot@wide@The two fully clothed adult women walk toward the court entrance together.

9|records-room|-@insert@Two separate closed French case bundles rest on the desk beside a larger narrative volume, no readable names.|-@close_up@A plain wax-sealed roll is compared with an illustrated abstract chronicle page, no combat or portrait.|-@insert@The roll is tied securely while the narrative volume remains open, clearly different types of evidence.|-@medium@The records desk shows the two bundles and book against its quiet shelves, no people or recreated famous duel.

10|records-room|-@insert@An open register has abstract entries beside a separate closed personal-looking letter.|Clerk@medium@Clerk examines a bundle and turns to an empty space on the desk.|-@close_up@A blank sheet lies where a missing personal statement could have been, an editorial object metaphor only.|-@insert@The blank sheet and surviving bound register remain separate, no invented testimony or named portrait.

11|records-room|-@insert@A generic painted theatre curtain sketch in a later plain book sits apart from the sealed case rolls.|-@close_up@The page contains only a simple curtain sketch, no film actor or real person's face.|Clerk@medium@Clerk closes the illustrated volume and returns attention to the case bundle.|-@insert@The source roll is foregrounded, with the closed storybook farther away on the same desk.

12|records-room|-@wide@The records shelves contain many quiet tied bundles rather than a staged battlefield.|-@insert@One small inquiry bundle is opened at the desk with quill and inkpot.|Clerk@medium@Clerk patiently compares individual sheets from that single bundle.|-@close_up@Two thin sheets and a tied roll form an ordinary procedural file, no swords or spectacle.

13|court-street|Margot@medium@Margot stands outside the court door with her papers held securely.|Agnes,Margot@medium@Agnes asks Margot a supportive practical question on the bench.|Margot@close_up@Margot listens thoughtfully to a different opinion off frame.|Agnes,Margot@wide@Agnes remains beside Margot as they prepare another visit, no hostile crowd.

14|town-court|Judge@medium@Judge studies a plain law book on the back bench.|-@insert@An unlettered royal wax seal is shown beside the folded petition, no national logo.|Clerk@medium@Clerk records a formal entry in the desk register.|Margot@close_up@Margot watches seriously, her own small bundle of papers held at her waist.

15|records-room|-@insert@Two different plain-bound legal books sit beside a local inquiry roll.|-@close_up@One book is open to abstract lines while the other remains closed, no quotations.|Clerk@medium@Clerk compares the book with the actual case sheet at the desk.|-@insert@The practical inquiry roll is placed separately from the two legal volumes, showing distinct kinds of source.

16|town-court|Clerk,Margot@medium@Clerk asks Margot to clarify a point and listens rather than interrupting.|Clerk@insert@Clerk's quill pauses over the entry, no readable names or modern forms.|Judge@close_up@Judge examines a separate paper thoughtfully.|Margot@medium@Margot answers with a small measured hand gesture and composed posture.

17|town-court|-@insert@Two short written entries with abstract marks lie next to each other on the clerk's desk.|Clerk@close_up@Clerk compares the two entries carefully.|Clerk,Margot@medium@Clerk turns back toward Margot with one questioning open hand.|Margot@close_up@Margot calmly clarifies her account, no reenactment, distress spectacle or physical contact.

18|records-room|-@insert@An independent Dijon-style late-medieval inquiry bundle lies on the records desk, no readable date or named portrait.|-@close_up@Several separate witness sheets are arranged around the opened bundle.|Clerk@medium@The fictional clerk illustrates the act of recording a statement, not a portrait of Borestal.|-@insert@The quill, fresh testimony sheet and closed prior bundle remain clearly distinct.

19|court-street|Margot,Agnes@medium@The adult fictional guides discuss whether to return to the court, with the petition between them.|Margot@close_up@Margot considers the practical decision, no tears or visible injury.|Agnes@close_up@Agnes listens without telling Margot what to do.|Margot,Agnes@wide@Margot takes one resolved step toward the doorway while Agnes offers calm company.

20|records-room|-@insert@Three separate case bundles sit across the desk with visible gaps, no connecting arrow or merged file.|-@close_up@The centre bundle has a closed register beside it, while the third has loose sheets; no readable words.|Clerk@medium@Clerk works on one bundle at a time and keeps the others tied.|-@wide@The three bundles remain separate in the quiet records room, no historical people reenacted.

21|court-street|Margot@medium@Margot leaves the doorway after a visit with one folded response in hand.|-@insert@The closed response and plain empty purse rest on the public bench, symbolic props not a claimed payout.|Margot,Agnes@medium@Agnes listens as Margot considers the response and what it means for her daily life.|Margot@close_up@Margot looks toward the street ahead, thoughtful rather than magically relieved.

22|records-room|-@insert@The first bundle is reopened beside a second inquiry sheet, recalling continuation after an obstacle.|-@close_up@The second bundle remains tied next to a blank personal sheet, recalling a missing voice.|-@insert@The third bundle contains several separate testimony sheets, without invented readable text.|-@medium@All three distinct bundles remain on the desk as an illustrative comparison, not one legal procedure.

23|town-court|Margot,Clerk@medium@Margot waits until Clerk finishes writing before asking another question.|Clerk@close_up@Clerk sets the quill down in the inkpot stand.|Margot@close_up@Margot asks what is expected of her next with a practical open hand.|Clerk,Margot@medium@Clerk listens attentively while Margot continues, no smiling promise of a guaranteed verdict.

24|records-room|-@insert@A fresh neutral research note lies beside the older case bundle, no readable claim.|Clerk@medium@Clerk checks the note against the preserved source roll.|-@close_up@The old sheet is left intact while the new note remains a separate document.|-@insert@A tied source bundle rests safely beside a separate folded parchment note, no modern notebook, electronics or labels.

25|records-room|-@insert@A sealed outcome roll rests beside an empty small purse, no implied completed payment.|-@close_up@An untied witness-sheet bundle and a closed narrative book remain distinct sources.|Clerk@medium@Clerk checks which document belongs to which bundle before replacing it.|-@wide@The ordered records desk is left quiet, with each bundle separate and no fabricated final verdict.
